title: Settings

workspace.heading: Workspace
workspace.ownersOnly: Only owners can rename the workspace.
workspace.description: The name and basic settings of this workspace.
workspace.nameDescription: Shown in the sidebar, in invitations and in emails.

export.heading: Export
export.title: Export workspace
export.description: Download every page you can see as a ZIP: pages as Markdown, databases as CSV, and the files they show. Pages in the trash are left out; templates are kept in a Templates folder.
export.disabled: Export is turned off for this workspace in Settings → Security.

members.heading: Members
members.description: Members can see and edit every page unless its sharing is restricted; guests see only pages shared with them. Owners can also manage members.

joinLink.heading: Add members with a link
joinLink.descriptionOn: Anyone who opens this link and signs in joins as a member, or with the role of a pending invitation for their email. Only owners can see it.
joinLink.descriptionOff: Turn on a link that anyone can use to join this workspace as a member.
joinLink.regenerateBody: The current link stops working right away. People who already joined keep their access.
joinLink.descriptionAsks: Anyone who opens this link and signs in asks to join, and an owner approves each request. People with a pending invitation join right away. Only owners can see it.

members.transferBody: {name} becomes an owner and you become a member. Only an owner can make you an owner again.
members.leaveBody: You lose access to its pages. Pages only you could manage pass to an owner. An owner can add you again.
members.removeBody: {name} loses access to this workspace right away, including in open pages and connected apps. Pages only they could manage pass to you.
members.expired: Link expired. Invite again for a new one.

add.title: Add members
add.description: People whose account has a verified address are added right away. Everyone else gets an invitation link.
add.count: {count, plural, =0 {Separate addresses with commas, spaces or new lines. Up to 50 at a time.} one {# address} other {# addresses}}
add.linkValidity: Invitation links work for 7 days and only for the invited email address.
add.descriptionAsks: An owner approves each address before anyone is added or invited.
add.requestedNote: Owners see your request in Settings > Members. Invitations go out once they approve.

guests.heading: Guests
guests.description: Guests are people from outside the workspace who see only the pages shared with them. See what each guest can open, take access back, make a guest a member or remove them.
guests.descriptionMember: Guests are people from outside the workspace who see only the pages shared with them. You can take back access on pages you have full access to. Only owners can make a guest a member or remove them.
guests.count: {count, plural, =0 {No guests} one {# guest} other {# guests}}
guests.empty: No guests yet. Sharing a page with the email address of someone outside the workspace adds them as a guest.
guests.noMatches: No guests or pages match your search.
guests.pageCount: {count, plural, =0 {No pages} one {# page} other {# pages}}
guests.hidden: {count, plural, one {# more page you don't have access to} other {# more pages you don't have access to}}
guests.makeMemberBody: {name} can then open the workspace's pages like any member, not only the pages shared with them, and join teamspaces.
guests.removeBody: {name} loses access to this workspace right away, including in open pages and connected apps. Pages only they could manage pass to you.
guests.revokeBody: The invitation link stops working, and the pages shared with {email} stop waiting for them.

teamspaces.heading: Teamspaces
teamspaces.description: Teamspaces group pages and the people working on them. Everyone sees the teamspaces they are in in their sidebar. Guests are never in teamspaces; they only see pages shared with them.
teamspaces.listDescription: Manage all the teamspaces you have access to here.
teamspaces.leaveBody: Its pages leave your sidebar. You can join an open teamspace again yourself; otherwise one of its owners has to add you.
teamspaces.archiveBody: It leaves everyone's sidebar and takes no new pages. You can restore it from the archived teamspaces.

defaults.heading: Default teamspaces
defaults.description: Everyone in the workspace is in these teamspaces and can't leave them, including people who join later. There is nothing to update when someone joins. New top-level pages go to the oldest one.
defaults.empty: No default teamspaces. New top-level pages go to people's private pages.
defaults.makeBody: Everyone in the workspace, now and later, is in it and can't leave it. Its pages appear in everyone's sidebar.
defaults.removeBody: Everyone stays in it for now but can leave it, and people who join the workspace later aren't added.

creation.title: Only workspace owners can create teamspaces
creation.description: Off: owners and members can create teamspaces. Guests never can.
creation.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can change this.

groups.heading: Groups
groups.description: Groups bundle people so you can share a page with all of them or add them to a teamspace at once. Whoever joins a group gets what the group has; whoever leaves it loses it. Only owners and members can be in groups, not guests.
groups.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can create and change groups.
groups.emptyOwner: No groups yet. Create one to share pages with several people at once.
groups.memberCount: {count, plural, =0 {No members} one {# member} other {# members}}
groups.name: Name
groups.deleteBody: Its members keep the access they have on their own. What the group was given on pages and in teamspaces goes away, and open pages they can no longer see close. Pages only the group could manage pass to you.

members.title: Members of {name}
members.empty: No one is in this group yet.
members.noOneToAdd: Every owner and member of the workspace is already in this group.
members.provisionedHint: Your identity provider manages this group over SCIM. Changes made here may be undone at its next sync.

errors.nameTaken: Another group already has this name.
errors.notMember: Only owners and members of the workspace can be in its groups.
errors.accessDenied: Only workspace owners can change groups.

agents.heading: Agents
agents.description: Agents are AI helpers with instructions of their own. An automation runs one on a database’s rows: it reads only what is shared with it, changes the row and comments on it, under its own name.
agents.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can create agents.
agents.emptyOwner: No agents yet. Create one, or start from a template below.
agents.restoreHint: A restored agent starts paused, with nothing shared with it.
agents.aiOff: AI is off in this workspace (Settings > General), so agents don’t run.
agents.aiUnavailable: AI isn’t set up on this server, so agents don’t run.
agents.archiveBody: It stops running and loses every page shared with it. Automations that run it skip it until it’s restored. What it changed and wrote keeps its name.

form.name: Name
form.descriptionPlaceholder: What it does, in a sentence
form.instructionsPlaceholder: For example: Read the new request. Set Team to Billing for questions about money, to Support otherwise. Explain your choice in a comment.
form.instructionsHelp: What the agent does whenever it runs: what to look at, what to change, what to write. It sees only the pages shared with it.
form.activeHelp: A paused agent’s runs end without doing anything.
form.webAccessHelp: It can open public web pages whose links it’s given or finds in the workspace. Turn it off for strictly internal jobs.
form.webAccessHelpSearch: It can search the web and open public web pages. Turn it off for strictly internal jobs.
form.limitHelp: The most tokens its runs may use in a calendar month (UTC). Once they reach it, its runs stop until the next month.
form.modelHelp: The fast model costs less and suits routine, well-defined jobs, such as summaries or sorting rows. The main model suits work that needs judgment.
form.limitInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 1,000,000,000, or leave it empty for no limit.
form.archivedNote: Restore the agent to change it.
form.helpersHelp: During a run it can hand part of its task to these agents, up to {max} times, and use their answers. Each works with its own access, tools and limits, and can’t ask other agents in turn.
form.helpersEmpty: There are no other agents in this workspace yet.
form.limitOwnersOnly: Only workspace owners set this limit.

describe.title: Describe an agent
describe.hint: Say what it should do, and AI drafts it for you to review.
describe.label: What should this agent do?
describe.placeholder:
For example:
– Every Monday at 9:00, summarize last week’s new rows in Tasks and comment the summary on the Weekly page.
– When a support request is added, look for the answer in the Help pages and comment it.
– Every morning, mark tasks whose due date has passed as Late.
describe.help: Nothing is saved yet: you check the draft and change what you like before creating the agent.
describe.reviewHint: AI can make mistakes. Check everything before you create it.
describe.pagesHelp: Shared with the agent when you create it, each at the access shown.
describe.noPages: No pages to share. You can share some later on its Access tab.
describe.setUpHelp: Created with the agent. Remove what you don’t want.
describe.setUpHelpShares: Created with the agent. Remove what you don’t want. An automation shares its database with the agent to edit.
describe.noSetUp: Nothing runs it on its own yet. Add a schedule later, or run it from a database automation.

triggers.rowCreated: When a row is added to {database}
triggers.propertyChanged: When {property} changes in a row of {database}
triggers.datePassed: Rows of {database}: {days, plural, =0 {when {date} is reached} one {# day after {date}} other {# days after {date}}}

access.description: The agent opens only these pages, and the pages and rows under them. On a run started by someone’s change, it opens only what that person can open too.
access.warning: Anything you share with an agent can end up in the rows it changes or the comments it writes, where everyone who can see those rows can read it.
access.empty: Nothing is shared with this agent yet.
access.hidden: {count, plural, one {# more page you can’t open is shared with it.} other {# more pages you can’t open are shared with it.}}
access.archived: An archived agent has nothing shared with it.
access.noPages: No other page you have full access to.
access.fullOnly: You can share pages you have full access to.
access.automationNote: An automation that runs this agent gives it edit access to its database when it’s saved.

skills.description: Skills are pages with instructions the agent follows on every run, after its own instructions, in this order. A run started by someone’s change, or by an answer to a public form, only uses the skills that person (or the form’s publisher) can open: share a skill with them at view to include it.
skills.rule: An agent only follows skills that no one but the workspace owners can edit. If a member, teamspace, group, guest or agent can edit one later, runs leave it out and say so in their steps.
skills.empty: This agent has no skills yet.
skills.hidden: {count, plural, one {It has # more skill you can’t open.} other {It has # more skills you can’t open.}}
skills.archived: Restore the agent to give it skills.

status.notASkill: Left out: no longer a skill
status.editable: Left out: someone besides the owners can edit it
status.tooLong: Left out: too long to fit with the skills above it

skills.noSkills: No other skill you can open.
skills.full: An agent can have at most {max} skills.
skills.libraryNote: Skills are made in the <link>skills library</link>.

memory.description: Notes that go with every run of this agent, so it doesn’t have to learn the same things again. Its runs propose notes; none goes with a run until an owner keeps it.
memory.rule: A run reads rows, pages and events other people and services wrote, and a note could carry their words into every later run. Read each proposal before you keep it. Kept notes go with every run, whoever starts it.
memory.off: AI memory is off in this workspace: runs carry no notes and propose none until an owner turns it on in <link>Settings → General</link>.
memory.archived: Restore the agent to change its memory.
memory.proposedHeading: {count, plural, one {# note to review} other {# notes to review}}
memory.empty: Nothing yet. Keep a note its runs propose, or write one here.
memory.hiddenText: Proposed on a row you can’t open.
memory.hiddenOthersText: Proposed by a run another owner started.
memory.fromHiddenRow: From a run on a row you can’t open
memory.fromRequest: From a run an owner asked for
memory.addPlaceholder: e.g. Refunds over 100 EUR go to the Billing team
memory.fullToKeep: The memory is full ({max} notes): delete a note to keep another.
memory.waiting: {count, plural, one {# note to review} other {# notes to review}}
memory.toReview: {count, plural, one {# note to review} other {# notes to review}}

runs.description: Its latest runs, kept for {days} days.
runs.requestedBy: asked by {name} ({via, select, api {API} other {AI assistant}})
runs.fromScheduleHidden: On a schedule · a database you can't open
runs.fromMention: Mentioned by {name} in a comment on {page}
runs.fromMentionHidden: Mentioned by {name} in a comment on a page you can’t open
runs.noSteps: It didn’t search, read or change anything.
runs.commentHidden: Commented on a row you can’t open

reason.aiOff: AI is off in this workspace.
reason.agentDisabled: The agent was paused or archived.
reason.noAccess: The agent, or the person whose change started the run, can’t open the row or its database.
reason.databaseGone: The database it looks after was deleted or moved to the trash.
reason.commentGone: The comment that mentioned it was deleted, or its page was moved to the trash.
reason.tooManyAttempts: It couldn’t start in time: the workspace’s AI allowance stayed used up.
reason.approvalTimeout: No one answered its call within a day, so nothing was sent.
reason.connectionGone: The connection that started it was removed.
reason.limitReached: It had used the agent’s monthly token limit.
reason.costLimit: The workspace had reached its monthly AI cost limit.

runs.waiting: It waits for an owner to answer this call:

tool.declined: Its call of “{tool}” on {connection} was declined; nothing was sent
tool.redo: Its call of “{tool}” on {connection} was sent back; nothing was sent
tool.expired: Its call of “{tool}” on {connection} ran out of time; nothing was sent

skipped.notASkill: Left out <name></name>: it’s no longer a skill
skipped.editable: Left out <name></name>: someone besides the owners can edit it
skipped.tooLong: Left out <name></name>: it didn’t fit in what a run can read
skipped.hidden: Left out <name></name>: the person who started the run can’t open it
skipped.removed: Left out <name></name>: an owner took it from the agent while the run waited

handoff.waiting: Asked <agent></agent>; it hadn’t finished when this run went on: “{task}”
handoff.limitReached: Couldn’t ask <agent></agent>: it has used its monthly token limit

runs.yoursOnly: You see the runs you started.
runs.waitingForOwner: A workspace owner answers this call.

usage.limitReached: Limit of {limit} reached: runs stop until next month

templates.heading: Start from a template
templates.description: Ready-made agents for a database. Most run on every new row, the wins logger on a connection’s events; you choose the database and what it uses.

wizard.title: Set up {name}

steps.connection: Choose where its events come from

wizard.chooseDatabase: Which database should it work on? You need full access to it.
wizard.noDatabases: No database you have full access to.
wizard.chooseLog: Which database should it add wins to? The Wins log template makes one. You need full access to it.
wizard.connectionHelp: It reads each event this connection receives and adds a row only when the event is a win or praise.
wizard.noConnections: This workspace has no connections yet, so nothing can send the agent events. <link>Add a connection</link> (Slack, GitHub, or your CRM or email through a signed webhook), then set the agent up.
wizard.eventTypeHelp: Only events of this type start it: “message” for Slack messages, “pull_request” for GitHub pull requests. Leave it empty for every event.
wizard.routerPropertiesHelp: Up to {max}. For a select or status it picks one of the options; for a person, someone of the workspace.
wizard.rulesPlaceholder: Questions about invoices or refunds: Category is Question. Anything broken: Category is Problem, Assignee is Deniz.
wizard.rulesHelp: In your own words: how to fill each property, and when.
wizard.answerPropertyHelp: A select or status it sets once it has answered, or when a person needs to step in.
wizard.needsPerson: When a person needs to step in
wizard.newOptionsNote: The new property gets the options “{answered}” and “{needsPerson}”.
wizard.flagPropertyHelp: Ticked on a new row that looks like others.
wizard.knowledgeHelp: Up to {max}, shared with the agent to view. It answers only from these pages.
wizard.noPages: No page you have full access to.
wizard.name: Agent name
wizard.summary: Creating it adds the agent and an automation on {database} that runs it on every new row. The agent gets edit access to {database}.
wizard.summaryPages: The pages you chose are shared with it to view.
wizard.summaryEvents: Creating it adds the agent and a trigger on {connection} that runs it on each event. The agent gets edit access to {database}.
wizard.summaryApproval: Each row it adds waits for an owner’s approval in the inbox.
wizard.logFillsNone: The log has none of the properties it fills (lists, dates, links, people, text); it adds each win’s title and text only.
wizard.chooseCompanies: Which database of companies or customers should it fill in? You need full access to it.
wizard.companyPropertiesHelp: Up to {max}. On a new row it fills only those still empty, never changing a value. A property’s description tells it what goes there; untick the ones it should leave alone.
wizard.noCompanyProperties: This database has no property it can fill: text, a link, an email, a phone number, a number, or a select with options. Add one, then set the agent up.
wizard.companyAutofilled: Left out, as AI autofill fills them: {properties}.
wizard.summaryWeb: It gets web access, to look the companies up.

errors.tooMany: A workspace can have at most {max} agents.
errors.archived: Restore the agent to change it.
errors.notAPage: This page can’t be shared with the agent: you need full access to it.
errors.tooManySkills: An agent can have at most {max} skills.
errors.skillEditable: Someone besides the workspace owners can edit “{title}”. An agent only follows skills that just owners can change: limit who can edit the page first.
errors.accessDenied: You don’t have permission to do this.

reasons.name: Give the agent a name.
reasons.icon: An agent’s icon is an emoji.
reasons.level: An agent can view, comment on or edit a page.
reasons.database: Choose a database of this workspace.
reasons.property: Choose properties of the right type.
reasons.option: Choose two different options of the property.
reasons.limit: Enter a token limit as a whole number from 1 to 1,000,000,000.
reasons.task: Write the task it does on each run.
reasons.taskLength: A task can have at most 2,000 characters.
reasons.repeat: Check when it repeats and its time zone.
reasons.helpers: Choose up to 10 other agents of this workspace that aren’t archived.
reasons.shareLevel: Choose full access, can edit or can view & interact.

errors.noteEmpty: Write what the agent should remember.
errors.noteTooLong: A note can have at most {max} characters.
errors.memoryFull: An agent keeps at most {max} notes. Delete one first.
errors.paused: Turn the agent on to run it.
errors.aiOff: AI is off in this workspace.
errors.limitReached: The agent used its monthly token limit ({limit} tokens).
errors.tooManyRuns: {max} runs asked of this agent are still waiting. Try again once one finishes.
errors.notADatabase: Choose a database of this workspace that you can open.
errors.tooManySchedules: There's no room for another schedule (at most {max}).
errors.notAllowed: Your access to this agent doesn’t allow this.
errors.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners change an agent’s monthly token limit.
errors.notAMember: An agent can be shared only with the workspace’s owners, members and groups.

connections.description: The tools of each connection this agent may use. Tools that only read run at once, except on a row from an anonymous form answer; any other waits for an owner’s approval every time the agent calls it.
connections.empty: No connections yet. Owners add them in <link>Settings › Connections</link>.
connections.notReady: This connection isn’t ready (it needs a sign-in or fails), so the agent can’t use its tools for now.
connections.ownersChoose: The tools of each connection this agent may use. Only workspace owners choose them.
connections.none: This agent can’t use any connection’s tools.

schedules.description: Let this agent run on its own, on a schedule: each run does the task, on the database you choose if any, and you get its report in your inbox. Its runs can open only what you can open.
schedules.agentPaused: The agent is paused: its schedules skip their runs until you turn it on.
schedules.archived: Restore the agent to change its schedules.
schedules.empty: No schedules yet. Add one, for example every morning at 8:00 to go through a board.
schedules.lastFailed: Its last run couldn't start; it tries again next time.

paused.runAsGone: Paused: the account of the person who set it is gone. Save it to run it as you.
paused.accessLost: Paused: the person who set it is no longer an owner or can't open the database. Save it to run it as you.
paused.failed: Paused: its last run couldn't start.

access.none: The agent can't open this database: it skips its runs until you share it in the Access tab.
access.view: The agent can only view this database: give it edit access in the Access tab to change rows.
access.comment: The agent can only comment on this database: give it edit access in the Access tab to change rows.

schedules.databaseHint: Each run reads this database first and may change and comment on its rows (at most {max} changes a run).
schedules.noDatabaseHint: Without a database it changes nothing: it reads what is shared with it and reports.
schedules.taskPlaceholder: e.g. Go through every row. Set Status to Late where the due date has passed, and list what I need to do today.
schedules.taskKept: You can't open the database, so you can't read the task. Leave this empty to keep it, or write a new one.
schedules.reportHint: When a run ends, its report comes to your inbox.

history.description: Each saved change to this agent’s settings, skills, schedules or shared pages makes a version. Changes you save within two minutes of each other count as one. The last {max} versions are kept.
history.compareNote: What changed from this version to the agent’s current setup. Restoring brings back what this version had.
history.same: This version is the same as the agent’s current setup.
history.sameLatest: This is the agent’s current setup.
history.reordered: The order of the skills changed.
history.taskHidden: The task is hidden: you can’t open its database.
history.confirmRestore: Restore version {number}? The agent’s settings, skills, schedules and shared pages go back to how they were then. Its runs, memory and usage stay as they are, and you can undo this by restoring a later version.
history.archived: Restore the agent to bring back one of its versions.

skipped.scheduleHidden: A schedule on a database you can’t open

reasons.invalid: the saved value isn’t valid any more
reasons.noAccess: you need full access to it
reasons.skillEditable: someone besides the owners can edit it

share.description: Who can use this agent, and what they can do with it.

levelHelp.full: Everything, including sharing and archiving it
levelHelp.edit: Change its settings, pages, skills, memory and schedules
levelHelp.interact: See it, chat with it and mention it in comments

share.readOnly: Only people with full access change who this agent is shared with.
share.archived: Restore the agent to change who it is shared with.
share.ownersKeep: Which connections’ tools it may use and its monthly token limit stay with the workspace’s owners.
share.groupMembers: {count, plural, =0 {Group with no members} one {Group of # member} other {Group of # members}}

agents.viewOnly: You can view this agent, chat with it and mention it. To change it, ask someone who can edit it.

creation.title: Only workspace owners can create agents
creation.description: Off: members can create agents too, and get full access to the ones they create. Guests never can.
creation.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can change this.

analytics.description: How much people edited in this workspace, counted from page history and each page's latest change. Nothing extra is tracked. Only owners see this.
analytics.howCounted: An edit is a saved version of a page (at most one every 10 minutes while someone types, and one before each app, AI or restore change) or a change page history doesn't keep, such as a row's values.
analytics.peopleDescription: Guests are listed with their edits but don't count as active members.
analytics.pagesDescription: Pages you can't open are counted but not named.
analytics.exportPeople: Download edits per person as CSV
analytics.exportPages: Download most edited pages as CSV

aiUsage.description: What this workspace's AI cost, by month, feature and model, and the most it may cost in a month. Only counts are kept, never what was asked or answered. Only owners see this.
aiUsage.howCounted: Costs are worked out in US dollars from the AI provider's prices as each request is answered, so they can differ slightly from its invoice. Models without known prices count at no cost; speech to text and embeddings are counted but not priced. Months follow UTC.
aiUsage.reachedWorkspace: This workspace reached its monthly AI cost limit. AI requests are refused until next month, or until an owner raises or removes the limit.
aiUsage.reachedServer: This workspace reached the server's monthly AI cost limit. AI requests are refused until next month; the server's administrator can change the limit.
aiUsage.limitHelp: Once this month's AI cost reaches it, AI requests in this workspace are refused until the next month. It counts all of the workspace's AI, its own AI account included. Leave it empty for no limit.
aiUsage.serverLimit: The server also holds what its own AI key pays for each workspace to {limit} a month.
aiUsage.serverLimitOwnAccount: The server's limit of {limit} a month doesn't apply while the workspace uses its own AI account.
aiUsage.limitInvalid: Enter an amount in US dollars above 0 and at most {max}, or leave it empty.
aiUsage.monthsDescription: The last 12 months. Choose a month to see it by feature and model.
aiUsage.ownAccountShare: {cost} of it was paid by the workspace's own AI account.
aiUsage.empty: No AI requests in this month.
aiUsage.cacheTitle: Read from the prompt cache: {read} · Written to it: {write}

health.description: What is worth tidying among the pages you can open, checked each time you open this tab. Nothing changes until you fix it.
health.checked: {count, plural, one {# page checked.} other {# pages checked.}}
health.truncated: Only the most recently edited pages were checked: the workspace has more than one check looks at.
health.more: {count, plural, one {# more not shown.} other {# more not shown.}}

brokenLinks.title: Broken links
brokenLinks.description: Links and mentions in a page to a page in the trash or deleted for good.

orphans.title: Pages nothing leads to
orphans.description: Top-level pages with no pages inside them that no other page links to. Where another page writes the title, it can link it.
orphans.none: Every page is linked or sits under another page.

empty.title: Empty pages
empty.description: Pages with a title and nothing else: no body and no pages inside.

stale.title: Untouched pages
stale.description: Pages nobody edited in the last {months} months, longest untouched first. They may be out of date.

duplicates.title: Possible duplicates
duplicates.description: Pairs of pages that say nearly the same thing, compared by meaning. Read both before merging them.
duplicates.none: No pages say nearly the same thing.
duplicates.noEmbeddings: Not checked: this server has no embeddings model for comparing pages by meaning.
duplicates.aiOff: Not checked: AI is off in this workspace, so pages aren't compared by meaning.

brokenRelations.title: Broken relations

errors.gone: This was already fixed or changed meanwhile.

preferences.description: Your account's preferences: how Leafdesk looks in this browser and which emails you get.

theme.heading: Appearance
theme.label: Theme
theme.note: This setting only applies to this browser. With the system setting, the app turns light or dark along with your device.

contrast.label: Contrast
contrast.note: High contrast makes secondary text, lines and focus outlines stronger, in either theme. This setting only applies to this browser. With the system setting, it follows your device's option to increase contrast.

language.heading: Language
language.label: Interface language
language.note: This setting applies to this browser only. Emails to you are in the language you last picked or signed in with.

leaveWorkspace.title: Leave workspace
leaveWorkspace.description: You're a guest here and see only the pages shared with you. Leaving removes that access.

deleteWorkspace.heading: Deletion
deleteWorkspace.title: Delete workspace
deleteWorkspace.description: Deletes this workspace for everyone, with all its pages, databases, files and settings. This can't be undone.
deleteWorkspace.dialogBody: Every page, database, file, comment and setting in this workspace is deleted for every member, along with its agents, connections and audit log. Nobody can open it again and it can't be restored. Export it first if you want a copy.
deleteWorkspace.typeName: Type the workspace's name to confirm: {name}

copyManually: Copying isn't available here. Select the text and press Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac).

connectedApps.revokeError: Could not revoke access. Try again.

mcp.heading: Connect an AI assistant
mcp.description: Leafdesk has a built-in MCP server. Assistants that support remote MCP servers can search, read and edit your pages and databases after you sign in and approve access. Every edit an assistant makes is saved to page history first, so you can undo it.

claude.title: Claude
claude.body: Open Settings, then Connectors, choose Add custom connector and paste the server URL. Claude opens Leafdesk in your browser so you can sign in and allow access.

claudeCode.title: Claude Code
claudeCode.body: Run this in a terminal, then use /mcp inside Claude Code to sign in.

codex.title: Codex
codex.body: Run this in a terminal. Codex sees that Leafdesk uses OAuth and opens your browser so you can sign in and allow access; if that window gets closed, run codex mcp login leafdesk. Update Codex first: older versions can't finish signing in.

other.title: Other MCP clients
other.body: Add a remote server with the Streamable HTTP transport and the URL above. The client discovers sign-in through standard OAuth 2.1 metadata; it can register itself automatically or use a client ID metadata document. Choose read-only access on the approval screen if the client should not edit anything.

errors.notMember: This person is not a member.

errors.transferToGuest: Make them a member before making them owner.

errors.ssoFirst: Set up single sign-on and verify its domains first.

errors.invalidCalloutStyle: A callout style couldn’t be saved: check its key, name and icon.

security.description: Decide how people sign in, who can bring people into this workspace, what guests can do, what can leave it (exports, connected apps) and who can publish pages to the web. Only owners can change these settings.

requireTwoFactor.title: Require two-step verification
requireTwoFactor.description: Everyone must use an authenticator app or sign in with a passkey to open this workspace. People without either are asked to set one up first. Apps connected over MCP and REST API tokens are not affected.
requireTwoFactor.setUpFirst: Turn on two-step verification for your own account first.
requireTwoFactor.withoutCount: {count, plural, one {# person here hasn't set it up yet.} other {# people here haven't set it up yet.}}

accessRequests.title: Access requests
accessRequests.description: People who open a link to a page they can't see can ask for access, with a message. The people with full access to the page get the request. Off: they only see that they don't have access.

guestInvites.title: Who can invite guests
guestInvites.description: People outside the workspace join as guests when someone shares a page with them by email. They see only the pages shared with them.

guestPrivatePages.title: Guests can create private pages
guestPrivatePages.description: Guests can add pages at the top of the sidebar that only they can see, and share them like any page. Off: they only work in pages shared with them.

publishing.title: Who can publish to the web
publishing.description: Published pages can be read, and public forms filled in, by anyone with the link. Guests can never publish. Pages and forms already on the web stay there until someone turns them off. Off: nobody can publish, and pages, forms and the site already on the web stop working until publishing is turned back on.

publications.title: Published pages
publications.description: Every page of this workspace that is on the web. Owners can take any of them offline.
publications.privatePage: A page you don't have access to
publications.confirm: Unpublish this page? The link stops working for everyone.
publications.off: Publishing is turned off: none of these pages are on the web right now. They come back when publishing is turned on again, unless you unpublish them.

forms.title: Public forms
forms.description: Every form of this workspace that takes answers from the web. Owners can turn off any of them.
forms.empty: No forms take answers from the web.
forms.privateForm: A form you don't have access to
forms.name: {view} in {database}
forms.confirm: Turn off this form's public link? It stops working for everyone.
forms.stale: Takes no answers: whoever opened it lost access
forms.off: Publishing is turned off: none of these forms take answers right now. They come back when publishing is turned on again, unless you turn them off.

loginMethod.title: How members sign in
loginMethod.description: With single sign-on only, members must sign in through the identity provider to open this workspace. Owners and guests can still use any method, so a broken identity provider can't lock you out.
loginMethod.setUpFirst: Set up single sign-on below first.

sso.title: Single sign-on (SSO)
sso.description: Connect your organization's identity provider over OpenID Connect or SAML. People with an address in its verified domains can sign in with it; the first time, their account is created and they join as members.

setup.oidcRedirectUriHint: Add this as an allowed redirect (callback) URL of the client at your identity provider.

dns.body: To prove these domains are yours, add a TXT record for each at your DNS provider, then verify. Nobody can sign in with this connection until then.
dns.name: Name
dns.verified: Domains verified. Single sign-on is on.

form.issuerHint: The address its OpenID configuration is served under (…/.well-known/openid-configuration).
form.metadataKept: Leave empty to keep the stored metadata
form.certificateKept: Leave empty to keep the stored certificate
form.domainsHint: Separated by commas, for example example.com, example.org. Subdomains are included.

errors.invalidDomain: {detail} can't be used: enter your organization's own email domains (not public mail services like gmail.com).
errors.noDomains: Add at least one email domain.
errors.invalidIssuer: The issuer must be an https address.
errors.discoveryFailed: Couldn't read the provider's OpenID configuration at {detail}. Check the issuer address.
errors.invalidSaml: Paste the identity provider's metadata XML, or enter its SSO URL, entity ID and signing certificate.
errors.dnsMismatch: The TXT record for {detail} wasn't found or has a different value. DNS changes can take a while to show up.
errors.domainTaken: {detail} is already verified elsewhere on this server.

errors.limit: A workspace can have at most 20 SCIM tokens. Revoke one first.
errors.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can do this.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

scim.title: User provisioning (SCIM)
scim.description: Let your identity provider add, update and remove members, and manage member groups, over SCIM 2.0.
scim.managed: {count, plural, =0 {No one is managed over SCIM yet.} one {# person is managed over SCIM.} other {# people are managed over SCIM.}}
scim.tokensDescription: The identity provider sends one as a bearer token. Each works only for this workspace.

created.title: Copy your token
created.body: Paste it into your identity provider now. It won't be shown again.

errors.name: Give the token a name of at most 100 characters.
errors.limit: A workspace can have at most 20 SCIM tokens. Revoke one first.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

trashRetention.title: Delete pages in the trash after
trashRetention.description: Pages that have been in the trash this long are deleted for good, with their subpages and files. The trash shows how many days each page has left.

historyRetention.title: Page history
historyRetention.description: Earlier versions of a page are kept for {days} days, up to {count} per page. Saved versions and versions from before a restore are kept for {keptDays} days, and the latest version of a page always stays.

memberInvites.title: Who can add members
memberInvites.description: Owners can always add people. Members add people as members, never as owners.

allowedDomains.title: Allowed email domains
allowedDomains.description: People with an address on these domains, subdomains included, can join without an invitation once you verify the domain below. Public mail services like gmail.com can't be added.
allowedDomains.verifiedByEmail: Only verified addresses join on their own: new accounts get a verification link by email.
allowedDomains.verifiedByProvider: Only verified addresses join on their own. This server doesn't send email, so only accounts from Google, GitHub or single sign-on count as verified.
allowedDomains.unverified: Not verified: nobody joins through it yet
allowedDomains.dnsBody: To prove this domain is yours, add this TXT record at your DNS provider, then verify.

errors.notListed: {detail} is no longer one of the allowed domains. Reload the page.
errors.dnsMismatch: The TXT record for {detail} wasn't found or has a different value. DNS changes can take a while to show up.
errors.domainTaken: {detail} is already verified by another workspace on this server.
errors.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can do this.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

domainJoin.title: When someone from these domains signs in
domainJoin.description: This happens once per person: someone who left or was removed doesn't come back on their own.

joinRequests.title: Who can ask to join
joinRequests.description: Requests wait in Settings > Members for an owner to approve or decline.
joinRequests.allowed_domains: People with an allowed email domain
joinRequests.linkHint: The join link then asks an owner instead of adding people right away.

export.title: Allow export
export.description: Everyone in the workspace can download pages as Markdown, CSV or ZIP and print them to PDF. Off: those options are gone for everyone, owners included.

connectedApps.title: Connected apps and API tokens
connectedApps.description: What AI assistants and other apps connected over MCP, and REST API tokens, may do in this workspace. They never get more than the person who connected them. With no access, the workspace is hidden from them.

workspaceApps.title: Apps that reach this workspace
workspaceApps.description: AI assistants and other apps that people here connected over MCP, and their REST API tokens that can reach this workspace, with when each last did. Disconnecting one takes it from that person's account: it reaches none of their workspaces until they connect it again.
workspaceApps.empty: No one here has connected an app or made an API token that reaches this workspace.
workspaceApps.readsHere: Reads only here: connected apps may only read
workspaceApps.offHere: No access here: connected apps are off
workspaceApps.confirmEverywhere: {kind, select, api_token {Revoke {person}'s token {name}? It stops working in all their workspaces.} other {Disconnect {name} from {person}'s account? It loses access to all their workspaces until they connect it again.}}
workspaceApps.error: Could not disconnect it. Try again.
workspaceApps.gone: It's already disconnected, or no longer reaches this workspace.
workspaceApps.shown: Showing the {shown} used here most recently of {total}.

audit.description: A record of who changed what in this workspace: members and roles, invitations, sharing, teamspaces and groups, settings, security, pages created, moved, trashed and deleted, publishing, connected apps and exports. Only owners can see it.
audit.retention: Newest first. Events are kept for one year.

notifications.heading: Notifications
notifications.description: Choose what shows in your inbox and what also comes by email.
notifications.pushDescription: Push notifications come for what shows in your inbox, on the devices where you turn them on.
notifications.pushDeviceOff: Get a notification on this device for each new item in your inbox, even when Leafdesk is closed.
notifications.pushDeviceOn: On: this device shows a notification for each new item in your inbox, even when Leafdesk is closed.
notifications.pushDeviceBlocked: This browser blocks notifications from Leafdesk. Allow them in the site's settings in your browser, then come back here.
notifications.pushDeviceUnsupported: This browser can't receive push notifications. On iPhone and iPad, add Leafdesk to the Home Screen and open it from there.
notifications.pushDeviceError: Push notifications couldn't be changed on this device. Try again.
notifications.assignmentDescription: Someone assigns you to a person property in a database row.
notifications.shareDescription: Someone gives you access to a page.
notifications.commentDescription: Someone comments on a page you started a comment thread in or replied to.
notifications.mentionDescription: Someone mentions you on a page with @.
notifications.reminderDescription: A reminder you set on a date in a page, or one a database's date sends you, is due.
notifications.accessRequestDescription: Someone asks for access to a page you have full access to.
notifications.mailOff: This server can't send email right now, so none go out.
notifications.joinRequestDescription: Someone asks to join a workspace you own, or a member asks to invite someone.
notifications.automationDescription: A database automation lets you know about a row someone added or changed.
notifications.rowUpdateDescription: Someone else changes a database row you follow: one you created, are assigned to, commented on or were mentioned on, or chose to follow.
notifications.pageUpdateDescription: Someone else edits a page you watch: one you created or edited, chose to watch, or that is in a teamspace you watch. Emails about the same page come at most every few hours, and after a few a day the rest come together in one email.
notifications.rowEmailDescription: A message comes in on a database row: through your own mailbox, or on a row you follow or are assigned to. It is in a mailbox already, so it never comes by email again.
notifications.watchedDescription: Pages you chose to watch or edited, and teamspaces you watch. You also watch the pages you created. Watchers hear about edits and new comment threads.
notifications.watchedNone: You aren’t watching any pages yet
notifications.watchedNoneDescription: Watch a page from its ⋯ menu, or a whole teamspace from its menu in the sidebar. Pages you edit are watched for you.

site.description: Give this workspace's published pages one readable address, a home page and navigation between them.
site.heading: Site
site.notSetUp: This workspace has no site yet. Its published pages are reachable only through their own links.
site.slugHint: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, 3 to 40 characters.
site.titleHint: Shown at the top of every page of the site.
site.homeHint: The page the site's address opens. Only published pages can be picked.
site.confirmRemove: Take the site down? Its address stops working; each published page keeps its own link.
site.membersOnly: Only owners can change the site.
site.pagesDescription: Published pages the site lists, each with its subpages. Pages that aren't listed keep working through their own links but can't be reached from the site.
site.pagesEmpty: No pages are published yet. Publish a page from its Share menu first.
site.privatePage: A page you don't have access to

errors.tooShort: The address needs at least 3 characters.
errors.tooLong: The address can have at most 40 characters.
errors.invalid: Use lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens; start and end with a letter or number.
errors.reserved: This address is reserved. Pick another one.
errors.homeNotPublished: Pick a published page of this workspace that you can see.
errors.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can do this.

connections.heading: Connections
connections.description: Services your agents use: Slack, GitHub, a CRM, another Leafdesk… anything with a remote MCP server. Only owners see and manage them; which tools each agent may use is set on the agent. Which tools the AI chat may use is set on each connection, under Tools. (Programs that use Leafdesk: the ones reaching this workspace are under Security, the ones you connected yourself under My account › Connected apps.)
connections.approvalNote: Agents run tools that only read at once, except on a row from an anonymous form answer. Every other call waits for an owner’s approval in the inbox; unanswered for a day, nothing is sent.

notices.signedIn: Signed in. The connection’s tools are listed below.
notices.oauthFailed: The sign-in didn’t finish. Try again; if it keeps failing, check the address and that the service allows Leafdesk to sign in.

errors.blocked: That address is on a private network, which connections can’t reach.
errors.notMcp: That address doesn’t answer as an MCP server.
errors.unauthorized: The server didn’t accept the sign-in.
errors.tokenForNewUrl: A new address needs its token: paste it again.
errors.invalidClient: Paste the app’s client ID (and its secret, if it has one).
errors.clientForNewUrl: A new address needs its app: enter the client ID and secret again.
errors.needsClient: This service doesn’t let Leafdesk register itself. Create an app there and enter its client ID and secret in the connection’s settings.
errors.redirectRejected: This service doesn’t accept Leafdesk’s sign-in return address. Its admin needs to allow {address}, or create an app there and enter its client ID and secret in the connection’s settings.
errors.registrationRejected: This service turned down Leafdesk’s registration: “{reason}”. Create an app there and enter its client ID and secret in the connection’s settings.
errors.invalidTrigger: Pick an agent of this workspace.
errors.oauthFailed: Signing in didn’t work. Try again.

approval.decided: Someone already answered this call, or it ran out of time.
approval.forbidden: Only owners can answer an agent’s call.

connections.addDescription: Enter the address of the service’s MCP server. Leafdesk keeps its credentials sealed on the server; they are never shown again.

catalog.description: Pick a service and Leafdesk fills in its address and how to sign in, or add any other remote MCP server.

fields.name: Name
fields.urlHelp: Its MCP endpoint, usually ending in /mcp. Only https addresses on the internet.

authHelp.oauth: You sign in at the service; Leafdesk registers itself (or signs in as an app you registered there) and keeps the access it gets.
authHelp.token: Sent as a bearer token with every call.
authHelp.none: For servers that need no sign-in.

fields.tokenKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved one

presets.hmac: Leafdesk signature (Zapier, Make, n8n, your own)

fields.redirectUrlHelp: Add this to the app’s redirect (callback) URLs at the service.
fields.clientSecretOptional: Leave empty if the app has none
fields.clientRequired: {name} signs in only apps registered with it. Create an app there, give it the redirect URL below, then paste its client ID and secret.
fields.clientInstance: This instance signs in to {name} with its own app.
fields.clientOverride: Use an app of your own instead
fields.clientOptional: Sign in as an app registered with the service

statusErrors.unauthorized: The server didn’t accept the credentials. Sign in again or change the token.
statusErrors.notMcp: The address doesn’t answer as an MCP server.
statusErrors.timeout: The server took too long to answer.
statusErrors.oauth: Signing in didn’t work. Try again.
statusErrors.other: Something went wrong with this connection.

tools.description: Each tool is classed by what the server says of it: tools marked read-only run at once, all others wait for approval. Change a class if the server is wrong.
tools.notListed: Its tools are listed once the connection works.
tools.overridden: Classed by an owner, not as the server marked it
tools.chatAll: Use all of them in the chat
tools.chatDescription: Tick “In chat” to let the workspace's AI chat use a tool. The chat calls it with this connection's account for any member who asks (not guests); a tool that changes things asks that person first, every time.

addressHelp.hmac: Send events here as POST requests signed with the secret below, the way Leafdesk’s own webhooks sign: X-Leafdesk-Signature is t=TIME,v1=HMAC (TIME in Unix seconds, HMAC the hex HMAC-SHA256 of TIME, a dot and the body), X-Leafdesk-Event names the type and X-Leafdesk-Delivery gives an id.
addressHelp.slack: Paste this as the Request URL of your Slack app’s Event Subscriptions, and paste the app’s signing secret below.
addressHelp.github: Add a webhook with this payload URL, content type application/json and the secret below.

events.triggersHelp: Which agent runs when an event arrives. An event type like “issues” also takes “issues.opened”; leave it empty for every event.
events.trustedOff: Every call to a connected service, reading ones too, waits for an owner’s approval: anyone who can make the service send an event writes what the agent reads.
events.trustedOn: Reading tools run without asking. Turn this on only if no one outside your team can make this service send events (no public repositories, open channels or forms): an event’s text can talk the agent into reading what is shared with it and sending it out through a reading tool.
events.noAgents: Create an agent first, then choose it here.
events.promptPlaceholder: What the agent should do with the event

connections.reconnectNote: Changing the address or the sign-in signs the connection out; it is tried again when you save. A new address also needs the token again, lists its tools afresh and takes this connection's tools away from agents until you give them again. The chat loses them too.
connections.deleteBody: Its credentials, the tools agents had on it, its triggers and its events go with it. Calls waiting for approval fail without sending anything.

approval.notePlaceholder: Use the customer’s company name as the title
approval.notWhole: This call is longer than shown here, or holds values masked here. Open its run to see all of what would be sent before approving it.

email.heading: Email
email.description: Mail with the people in your databases lands on their rows: everyone who can see a row reads its mail there and answers it from their own mailbox.
email.enabledHint: Members connect their own mailbox under My account › Email and calendar. Only mail whose other party is a row's email address is ever read whole; the rest stays in the mailbox.
email.databasesDescription: A message goes to the row whose email property holds the other party's address, in the first of these databases where exactly one row does. Replies follow their thread.
email.databasesNoneHint: Add a database with an email property, such as your customers or contacts.
email.removeDatabase: Stop matching mail to this database
email.mailboxDescription: The mailbox you use in this workspace. It is read for mail with the people in the workspace's mail databases, and what you write on rows is sent from it. Your other workspaces don't see it.
email.folders: Reads incoming mail from {inbox} and sent mail from {sent}.
email.noSentFolder: Reads incoming mail from {inbox}. No sent folder was found, so mail you send from your own mail program won't show on rows, and mail sent from rows won't be saved in your mailbox.
email.consent: I understand that mail with the people in this workspace's mail databases, sent or received through this mailbox, shows on their rows to everyone who can see those rows.

error.blocked: The mail server is on a private network, which this server doesn't reach.
error.notFound: The mail server's name wasn't found.
error.auth: The mail server refused the user name or password. Check the app password.
error.tls: A secure connection to the mail server couldn't be made.
error.unreachable: The mail server can't be reached right now.
error.noInbox: The mail server shows no inbox.

fields.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the current one
fields.passwordHelp: An app password made for Leafdesk, not the password you sign in with. It is kept encrypted and never shown again.

providerHelp.google: Also for Google Workspace addresses on your own domain. Make an app password in your Google account under Security (2-Step Verification must be on).
providerHelp.yandex: Make an app password for mail in your Yandex ID settings.
providerHelp.zoho: Turn on IMAP access in Zoho Mail's settings and make an app password.

email.membersDescription: Who has connected a mailbox in this workspace. Nobody but its owner sees what is in it.

errors.disabled: Email on rows is off in this workspace.
errors.invalid: Some of the details aren't valid. Check them and try again.
errors.consent: Confirm that mail on rows shows to everyone who can see them.
errors.noMailbox: Connect your mailbox in Settings > Email and calendar first.
errors.rateLimited: Your mailbox has sent as much as it may this hour. Try again later.
errors.notFound: The mail server's name wasn't found.
errors.blocked: The mail server is on a private network, which this server doesn't reach.
errors.auth: The mail server refused the user name or password. Check the app password.
errors.tls: A secure connection to the mail server couldn't be made.
errors.unreachable: The mail server couldn't be reached. Check the server names and ports.
errors.noInbox: The mail server shows no inbox.
errors.accessDenied: You don't have access to do this.
errors.gone: That message isn't on this row any more.

storage.description: Where this workspace's uploaded files are kept: this server, or storage one of its owners connected to their account (an S3-compatible bucket, Google Drive or Dropbox). Leafdesk still serves every file itself, so the storage stays private: members need no account there, and no public access or sharing is needed.
storage.instanceHint: Files are kept on the server Leafdesk runs on.

kindHints.s3: AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, or any other storage that speaks the S3 protocol.
kindHints.gdrive: Files go in a Leafdesk folder Leafdesk makes in your Drive, with a folder for each workspace. Leafdesk can only see the files it made there, nothing else in your Drive.
kindHints.dropbox: Files go in Leafdesk's app folder in your Dropbox (under Apps), with a folder for each workspace. Leafdesk can't see anything outside it.

storage.files: {count, plural, =0 {No files yet} one {# file, {size}} other {# files, {size}}}
storage.noQuota: no storage limit of this server applies
storage.olderFiles: Files uploaded before it was connected stay on this server ({size}).
storage.disconnectNote: New files will go to this server again. Files already in that storage stay there and are still read from it until they are deleted or moved.

fields.endpointHint: The storage's S3 address, starting with https://. Leave it empty for AWS S3.
fields.regionHint: us-east-1 when unsure; auto for Cloudflare R2.
fields.prefixHint: Optional: files go under this folder of the bucket.
fields.keysHint: Give these keys access to this bucket only. They are stored encrypted and never shown again.
fields.pathStyleHint: Needed for MinIO and most storage other than AWS S3.
fields.label: Name
fields.labelHint: What you call this storage in Leafdesk. Optional.

storage.testOk: It works: a test file went there and back.
storage.retiredDescription: Storage this workspace used before that still holds files. They are read from there until they are deleted or moved.

errors.accessDenied: Only the workspace's owners can change where its files are stored.
errors.endpoint: Enter the endpoint as a web address, like https://storage.example.com.
errors.region: Enter a region of lowercase letters, digits and dashes, like us-east-1.
errors.bucket: Enter the bucket's name: 3 to 63 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores.
errors.prefix: A folder may only hold letters, digits, dashes and underscores, separated by slashes.
errors.unavailable: That kind of storage can't be connected yet.
errors.rateLimited: Too many tries. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
errors.noStorage: This workspace keeps no files in storage of its own.
errors.notConfigured: This server isn't set up for that kind of storage.
errors.oauthFailed: Signing in didn't work, so nothing was changed. Try again.
errors.disabled: This server doesn't let anyone connect storage of their own.
errors.noAccount: That storage isn't connected to your account.
errors.moveInProgress: This workspace's files are being moved. Wait for it to finish.
errors.noDestination: The files of {workspace} have nowhere to move to: no other owner has default storage, and this server's storage can't take them.
errors.serverRefused: This server's storage can't take this workspace's files: it isn't S3, or they don't fit the workspace's quota there.
errors.noMove: That move isn't there any more.

storage.signInHint: You sign in at {provider} and come back here. Before anything is saved, a test file is stored, read back and deleted.
storage.notConfigured: {provider} isn't offered: register an app with {provider} and set {vars} on the server to offer it.

notices.connected: Connected. New files go there from now on.
notices.refused: You signed in, but a test file couldn't be stored there, so nothing was changed. Try again later.

storage.descriptionOff: Where this workspace's uploaded files are kept. Some are in storage connected before this server stopped offering storage of one's own; nothing new can be connected.
storage.brokenHelp: Files stored there can't be read until it works again. If the storage is gone for good, restore the workspace from a backup.

owner.gone: Storage of someone who has left Leafdesk

storage.useDescription: New files go to storage you connected to your account, in a folder of this workspace's own. Before anything changes, a test file is stored, read back and deleted. Files already uploaded stay where they are until you move them.

move.heading: Move files
move.description: Copies every file of this workspace to other storage, a few at a time, while the workspace keeps working, then deletes them from where they were. New files go there from the start.
move.confirm: Move every file of this workspace to {destination}? New files go there from now on.
move.queued: Files are about to move to {destination}.
move.done: {files, plural, =0 {Done: new files go to {destination} now.} one {Moved # file to {destination}.} other {Moved # files to {destination}.}}
move.failed: {failed, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} couldn't be moved to {destination}: {error}
move.blocked: The storage holding this workspace's files is going away, and there is nowhere they may move to: no owner has default storage, and this server's storage can't take them. They are still read from it for now. Set up storage, then try again.
move.backupHint: Files that can't be read from their storage any more come back by restoring a backup of the workspace.

reasons.left: The storage holding these files belongs to someone who left the workspace.
reasons.removed: The storage holding these files belongs to someone who was removed from the workspace.
reasons.accountDeleted: The storage holding these files belongs to someone who deleted their Leafdesk account.
reasons.disconnected: The storage holding these files was disconnected by its owner.

accounts.heading: Connected storage
accounts.description: Storage you connect once and use in the workspaces you own: an S3-compatible bucket, Google Drive or Dropbox. Each workspace gets a folder of its own there; other members read its files through Leafdesk and need no account with the storage. For shared workspaces, prefer storage your team owns (a company bucket or shared account): if you leave one, its files have to move.
accounts.descriptionOff: Storage you connected earlier. This server no longer lets anyone connect new storage; workspaces using this keep working.
accounts.connected: Connected. Choose it in a workspace's Settings > Storage, or make it your default.
accounts.none: No storage connected yet. Files go to this server.
accounts.disconnected: Disconnected: still read from until its files are moved or deleted
accounts.disconnectUsed: These workspaces stop putting new files there. Their files move to another owner's storage where they can; the others are still read from it until they are moved or deleted.
accounts.disconnectUnused: No workspace uses it. Leafdesk forgets it and its keys.

backup.title: Back up workspace
backup.description: Download everything in the workspace as one file, to restore here or on another Leafdesk: pages with their history, databases, comments, files, teamspaces, groups and access, agents and automations. People's AI chats and what the AI remembers about them stay out.
backup.disabled: Backups are turned off together with export in Settings → Security.

calloutStyles.heading: Callout styles
calloutStyles.description: Named box styles everyone can insert from the / menu. Changing a style changes every callout that uses it.
calloutStyles.previewText: Text of a callout in this style.
calloutStyles.removeConfirm: Remove the style “{name}”? Callouts using it become plain callouts.
calloutStyles.ownersOnly: Only owners can change callout styles.
calloutStyles.name: Name
calloutStyles.keyHelp: Markdown writes it as > [!{key}]. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
calloutStyles.title: Default title
calloutStyles.titleHelp: Shown when a callout of this style has no title of its own.

problems.key: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
problems.reservedKey: This key is taken by a built-in kind (note, tip, important, warning, caution, info, danger, details, frame, card, panel).
problems.duplicateKey: Another style already has this key.
problems.name: Enter a name of up to 60 characters.
problems.icon: Choose one emoji, or no icon.
problems.title: Keep the title to 120 characters.
